product_family: Open-source low-code application platform for building internal tools (admin panels, dashboards, portals). Ships as free self-hosted Community Edition (Apache 2.0), paid self-hosted Business/Enterprise Editions with SSO/RBAC/audit logging, and a hosted Appsmith Cloud SaaS offering.

certifications.name: SOC 2 Type II
certifications.proof_quote:
SOC 2 Type II 

Proven security processes and controls.

certifications.name: SOC 2 Type II (trust center corroboration)
certifications.proof_quote: Trust center lists a "SOC 2" compliance badge and states: "We are working on our security compliance. We can provide completed questionnaires upon request."

certifications.name: ISO 27001
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence. Appsmith's own trust center states: "We are working on our security compliance. We can provide completed questionnaires upon request," and lists no ISO 27001 badge or report alongside its SOC 2 entry.

certifications.name: GDPR (posture)
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence of a formal GDPR-compliance statement or downloadable DPA. The privacy policy only references EU law generically: "This...does not apply, whenever the processing of Personal Data is subject to European data protection law," without naming GDPR, SCCs, or a DPA.

certifications.name: HIPAA
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence of HIPAA compliance or a BAA offering. Appsmith's own FAQ instead tells regulated customers to self-host: "If you want to...ensure HIPAA compliance, you can self-host Appsmith to ensure none of your data leaves your VPC."

certifications.name: PCI DSS
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence. Not mentioned on the trust center or security documentation; Appsmith does not process cardholder data as part of its product.

certifications.name: ISO/IEC 42001 (AI governance)
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence of an AI-management-system certification on the trust center or elsewhere on the vendor's domains.

privacy.ai_training_note: Appsmith's AI copilot forwards only relevant portions of user prompts/documents to third-party model providers (OpenAI, Anthropic). Appsmith's own blog states: "We only work with providers who pledge to never store or use our customers' data to train their AI models." This is a blog statement, not a formal DPA or subprocessor addendum.
privacy.data_region: Appsmith Cloud: hosted on AWS, data stored/processed in the US ("For Appsmith cloud users, data is stored and processed on servers in the US" - docs FAQ). Self-hosted editions (Community/Business/Enterprise): data stays entirely within the customer's own infrastructure/region of choice; Appsmith states it "does not store User data processed as part of its Services" for the core product.

security.name: Encryption in transit
security.value: All traffic to and from Appsmith Cloud is secured using TLS; self-hosted instances can configure SSL via Let's Encrypt or a custom certificate.

security.name: Encryption at rest
security.value: Sensitive data (database credentials, Git SSH keys) protected with AES-256 encryption; self-hosted deployments use a unique salt/password configuration.

security.name: SSO
security.value: SAML and OIDC SSO supported for secure authentication with the customer's identity provider.

security.name: Access control
security.value: Role-based access controls (RBAC) with granular roles, groups, and permissions; SCIM-based user provisioning from an IdP.

security.name: Audit logging
security.value: Audit logs to track organizational use and support incident remediation.

security.name: Account security
security.value: Two-factor authentication (2FA) available for Appsmith Cloud accounts, with internal access strictly regulated.

security.name: Application security testing
security.value: Every code commit is scanned by Snyk, Deepsource, and Dependabot; regular third-party vulnerability and penetration tests are conducted (reports available on request via the trust center).

security.name: Backend data handling
security.value: The Appsmith backend acts as a proxy and does not log or store data returned from connected databases/API endpoints.

products.name: Appsmith Community Edition
products.data_scope: Runs entirely on customer-owned infrastructure; no application data leaves the customer's environment.
products.notes: Free, Apache 2.0 licensed, community-supported. No SSO/SCIM/audit logging.

products.name: Appsmith Business / Enterprise Edition
products.category: Self-hosted low-code platform with enterprise controls
products.data_scope: Self-hosted (including air-gapped options); customer retains full control of data and region.
products.notes: Adds SAML/OIDC SSO, SCIM provisioning, RBAC, audit logging; covered by the same SOC 2 Type II report as Appsmith Cloud since the codebase is shared.

products.name: Appsmith Cloud
products.data_scope: Hosted on AWS; data stored and processed on US-based servers per Appsmith's own FAQ.
products.notes: Subject to Appsmith's SOC 2 Type II report. Docs page separately notes AWS's own SOC 1/SOC 2 attestation for the underlying data centers, which is the host's certification, not an additional Appsmith cert.

compare.pricing_model: Free open-source Community Edition; paid Business/Enterprise self-hosted tiers (license/seat-based); Appsmith Cloud SaaS subscription
compare.data_residency: Cloud: US-based AWS servers. Self-hosted: fully customer-controlled, any region, including air-gapped deployments.

flags: Docs page (docs.appsmith.com/product/security) states 'The cloud version of Appsmith is hosted on AWS data centers that adhere to SOC 1 and SOC 2 compliance standards' - this is AWS's (the host's) certification, distinct from Appsmith's own SOC 2 Type II report (Certpro-audited, announced 2022, listed on Appsmith's own trust center). Both are real but must not be conflated when listing the cert.

Third-party review sites (e.g., blaze.tech) claim Appsmith 'has security certifications that meet the requirements of SOC2, HIPAA, and GDPR,' but this is not corroborated on any appsmith.com, docs.appsmith.com, or security.appsmith.com page, and it contradicts Appsmith's own FAQ, which tells customers needing HIPAA-level control to self-host rather than claiming HIPAA compliance.

Appsmith's trust center (security.appsmith.com, SafeBase-hosted) explicitly states it is 'working on our security compliance' beyond SOC 2, confirming ISO 27001 and similar frameworks are not yet held.
The privacy policy is a generic template that references 'European data protection law' without naming GDPR explicitly or linking a standalone DPA. It does not amount to a GDPR certification claim.
The no-training claim comes from an Appsmith blog post, not a contractual DPA or subprocessor list.
